The distance to the Large Magellanic Cloud is approximately 150,000 light-years (a value often used in introductory physics problems, and hinted at by the aliens' 150-year average lifetime). The spacecraft travels at \(v = 0.99999987c\). For such high speeds, the Lorentz factor is

\[
\gamma = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}} \approx \frac{1}{\sqrt{2(1 - v/c)}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \times 1.3 \times 10^{-7}}} \approx 1961.
\]

In the Earth frame, the journey takes about \(150\,000\) years. From the astronaut's point of view, time dilation reduces the trip's duration to

\[
\Delta t_{\text{astronaut}} = \frac{150\,000 \text{ years}}{\gamma} \approx \frac{150\,000}{1961} \approx 76.5 \text{ years} \approx 77 \text{ years}.
\]

The astronaut begins at age 22, so they would be about 99 years old upon arrival—well within the 150-year average lifetime.
